newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers return to Joseph's tomb.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers return to Joseph's tomb.

text.p: Jewish settlers returned by armoured truck to the biblical Joseph's tomb in Palestinian- ruled Nablus on Sunday for the first time since bloody clashes two months ago, witnesses said.
Israeli soldiers and Palestinian police coordinated the return of the settlers who study at the West Bank shrine during the day before returning home.
Six Israeli soldiers died when Palestinian rioters and police besieged the tomb in the heart of Nablus on September 26.

The violence erupted throughout the West Bank and Gaza Strip over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to open an archaeological tunnel near an Islamic site in Jerusalem. Sixty Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers died in the bloodshed.
Some 25 settlers, wearing the skullcaps of religious Jews and some in religious prayer shawls, arrived on Sunday with a refrigerator. Some carried guns. They refrained from speaking to reporters.
Troops returned to the site the day after an Israeli force was trapped at the shrine, holy to Moslems and Jews. The six soldiers died in gunbattles with Palestinian police.
Nablus, occupied with the rest of the West Bank by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, was handed over to Palestinian self-rule on December 11, 1995, under an Israeli peace deal with the PLO.
